name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Oregon dairy-linked case 18 Nov; no human spread
summary: Oregon confirmed a mild dairy-linked H5N1 case on 18 Nov, the fourth US case since mid-Oct; no human spread
state: Oregon's state laboratory confirmed a human H5N1 case on 18 Nov in a person exposed to cattle at a Morrow County dairy farm; symptoms were mild, and officials said the virus is not known to spread between people (KVAL, 19 Nov). This follows three Yakima County, Washington, cases since 15 Oct, one fatal, also linked to dairy cattle (ECDC). Cases remain sporadic animal-to-human with no cluster under investigation, so the level stays Normal; the trend is rising.
for_you: The public risk is low. Farm and dairy workers in affected US states should follow CDC and state health guidance on protective equipment. In the UK, follow UKHSA advice and avoid touching sick or dead birds.
rubric_hit: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only (Normal): Oregon case 18 Nov dairy-linked, no human-to-human spread

sources.title: KVAL — Oregon health officials confirm human case of bird flu at Morrow County dairy farm

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
